sentences.text: Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 in connection with FIR No. 204/2022 dated ( not mentioned) registered at P.S -Kanadiya, Indore , District- Indore (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 420, 419, 406 of IPC.

2/ As per prosecution story, the complainant Mahendra Billore filed a complaint at the police station - Kanadiya, Indore by stating that the applicant had sold the. plot no. 70/1 Vaibhav Nagar,
Indore to him in the year 2008-09 for a sum of Rs. 8,00,000/-.
Later on, the complainant came to know that the said plot was mortgaged with the Allahabad Bank for a loan of Rs. 13,95,000/-.
When the complainant demanded the amount, the applicant sought time to pay the same and offered cheque on 20.02.2020 and on 18.03.2020.

When the complainant demanded the money, the Lokesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126636000/
1 applicant refused to give money and also abused and threatened to kill the complainant.

sentences.text: On the basis of the aforesaid, the present offence has been registered against the applicant 3/
Learned counsel for the applicant contended that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in this offence.
There is no legal evidence available on record to connect the applicant with the aforementioned offence.
Investigation is over and charge-sheet has been filed.
Evidence is goint on before the trial Court and material witness complainant Mahendra Bilore has been examined before the trial Court.
His earlier application was dismissed as withdrawn, but thereafter, during framing of charge, only charge under section 420 of IPC is framed against him.
No agreement to sale has been executed between them.
The applicant has already suffered jail incarceration for more than one year.
He is permanent resident of District- Indore.
There is no apprehension of his fleeing away from the court of justice.
Final conclusion of trial shall take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

4/ Per-contra, learned counsel for respondent - State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by stating that one another offence under section 138 of N.I. Act has already been registered against the applicant.
5/ Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case dairy.

6/ Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, arguments advanced by both the parties,
nature of allegation as also taking note of the fact that charge under section 420 of IPC is framed against the applicant, which is exclusively triable by JMFC; material witness has been examined before the trial Court; he is in custody for more than one year and possibility of delay in conclusion of the trial cannot be ruled out, in view of the evidence available on record, I deem it proper to release the accused / applicant on bail.
7/ Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.
75,000/- (Rs. Seventy Five Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.
8/ He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated u/S. 437(3) Cr.P.C., Certified copy, as per Rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE amol Lokesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126636000/
